name: Muhammad
note: The name of the Final Prophet (ﷺ). Most common Islamic name worldwide.

name: Ahmad
note: Another name of the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned in the Quran (61:6).

name: Ali
note: Name of the fourth Caliph and cousin of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Umar
note: Name of the second Caliph, Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضي الله عنه).

name: Uthman
note: Name of the third Caliph, Uthman ibn Affan (رضي الله عنه).

name: Abu Bakr
meaning: Father of the young camel; father of Bakr
note: Kunya of the first Caliph, Abdallah ibn Abi Quhafa (رضي الله عنه).

name: Ibrahim
note: Prophet Abraham (عليه السلام), called Khalilullah (Friend of Allah).

name: Ismail
note: Son of Prophet Ibrahim (عليه السلام), ancestor of the Arabs.

name: Yusuf
note: Prophet Joseph (عليه السلام), his story is told in Surah Yusuf.

name: Hassan
note: Grandson of the Prophet (ﷺ), son of Ali and Fatima.

name: Hussain
note: Grandson of the Prophet (ﷺ), son of Ali and Fatima, martyred at Karbala.

name: Abdullah
note: The name of the Prophet's (ﷺ) father. Most virtuous compound name.

name: Abdul Rahman
note: One of the most beloved names to Allah according to hadith.

name: Khalid
note: Name of the famous Companion and general Khalid ibn al-Walid.

name: Bilal
note: Bilal ibn Rabah (رضي الله عنه), the first muezzin of Islam.

name: Salman
note: Salman al-Farisi (رضي الله عنه), the Persian Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Tariq
note: Named after the star. Also the name of the Andalusian conqueror Tariq ibn Ziyad.

name: Zayd
note: Zayd ibn Haritha (رضي الله عنه), the adopted son of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Hamza
note: Uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ), known as the 'Lion of Allah', martyred at Uhud.

name: Musa
note: Prophet Moses (عليه السلام), most mentioned prophet in the Quran.

name: Isa
note: Prophet Jesus (عليه السلام), born of Maryam (Mary), called Ruhullah (Spirit of Allah).

name: Yahya
note: Prophet John the Baptist (عليه السلام), son of Zakariya.

name: Dawud
note: Prophet David (عليه السلام), king and prophet, to whom the Psalms (Zabur) were revealed.

name: Sulayman
note: Prophet Solomon (عليه السلام), son of Dawud, who was given power over jinn and animals.

name: Idris
note: Prophet Enoch (عليه السلام), mentioned in the Quran as a man of truth and a prophet.

name: Nuh
note: Prophet Noah (عليه السلام), builder of the Ark, one of the five Ulul Azm prophets.

name: Adam
note: The first human and first prophet (عليه السلام), created from clay by Allah.

name: Harun
note: Prophet Aaron (عليه السلام), brother and helper of Musa.

name: Ilyas
note: Prophet Elijah (عليه السلام), mentioned in the Quran as one of the righteous.

name: Zakariya
note: Prophet Zechariah (عليه السلام), father of Yahya.

name: Salih
note: Prophet Salih (عليه السلام), sent to the people of Thamud.

name: Hud
note: Prophet Hud (عليه السلام), sent to the people of 'Ad. A surah is named after him.

name: Shuaib
note: Prophet Shu'ayb (عليه السلام), sent to the people of Madyan.

name: Luqman
note: A wise man mentioned in the Quran, whose advice to his son forms Surah Luqman.

name: Ameen
note: A title of the Prophet (ﷺ) before prophethood. Means the Trustworthy One.

name: Anas
note: Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه), personal servant of the Prophet (ﷺ) for 10 years.

name: Qasim
note: Name of the Prophet's (ﷺ) first son, from whom his kunya Abu Qasim comes.

name: Talha
note: Talha ibn Ubaydillah (رضي الله عنه), one of the ten promised paradise.

name: Zubayr
note: Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam (رضي الله عنه), one of the ten promised paradise.

name: Muaz
note: Muaz ibn Jabal (رضي الله عنه), highly knowledgeable Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Walid
note: A classical Arabic name meaning one who is newly born or newly arrived.

name: Faisal
meaning: Decisive, separator of right from wrong
note: Carries the meaning of a judge or arbitrator who separates truth from falsehood.

name: Malik
note: Malik ibn Anas (رحمه الله), founder of the Maliki school of Islamic law.

name: Jamal
note: From the hadith: Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty.

name: Imran
note: The father of Maryam (Mary), mother of Isa (عليه السلام). Surah Al-Imran is named after his family.

name: Saad
note: Saad ibn Abi Waqqas (رضي الله عنه), one of the ten promised paradise.

name: Taha
note: Title of a surah (Surah 20). Often interpreted as a name or Quranic initials (huruf muqattaat).

name: Aziz
note: One of the 99 Names of Allah (Al-Aziz). Used as a personal name by Muslims.

name: Kareem
note: One of the 99 Names of Allah (Al-Kareem). Common personal name across the Muslim world.

name: Rashid
meaning: Rightly guided, on the right path
note: One of the 99 Names of Allah (Al-Rashid). Reflects guidance and righteousness.

name: Nasir
note: Reflects the concept of divine help and support in Islam.

name: Nabil
note: A name reflecting nobility of character and lineage.

name: Kamal
note: Represents the Islamic ideal of striving for excellence in character and deeds.

name: Ayman
note: Carries connotations of blessedness and good fortune.

name: Faris
note: Traditionally associated with chivalry, bravery, and nobility.

name: Ghalib
note: Reflects triumph and victory. Also the pen name of the great Urdu poet Mirza Ghalib.

name: Jafar
note: Jafar ibn Abi Talib (رضي الله عنه), cousin of the Prophet (ﷺ), martyred at Mu'ta.

name: Layth
note: A name symbolizing courage, strength, and bravery.

name: Mansur
note: Reflects divine aid and victory given by Allah to the believer.

name: Sabir
note: Sabr (patience) is among the highest virtues in Islam. Allah is with the patient.

name: Tawfiq
note: Refers to the success and guidance that comes from Allah alone.

name: Haidar
note: A title given to Ali ibn Abi Talib (رضي الله عنه) for his bravery.

name: Furqan
meaning: Criterion, separator of truth from falsehood
note: A name of the Quran mentioned in Surah Al-Furqan (25). Refers to discernment.

name: Rafiq
note: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Allah is Rafiq (gentle) and loves gentleness in all things.

name: Numan
note: Al-Numan ibn Bashir (رضي الله عنه), Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Rida
note: Represents the Islamic ideal of being content with Allah's decree (Ridha bil qadha).

name: Sufyan
note: Sufyan al-Thawri (رحمه الله), one of the greatest scholars of hadith.

name: Imad
note: Refers to being a pillar of strength and support.

name: Ghazi
meaning: Warrior, one who fights in the way of Allah
note: Historically given to warriors who fought for the defense of Islam.

name: Bakr
note: The name of a prominent Arab tribe. Abu Bakr's father's name was Abi Quhafa, but the kunya refers to Bakr.

name: Jabir
meaning: Comforter, one who sets bones, restorer
note: Jabir ibn Abdullah (رضي الله عنه), Companion who narrated many hadiths.

name: Kazim
meaning: One who controls anger, who swallows rage
note: The Quran (3:134) praises those who suppress their anger. A great virtue in Islam.

name: Rayan
note: One of the gates of Jannah mentioned in hadith, entered by those who fast.

name: Siraj
note: The Quran describes the Prophet (ﷺ) as Siraj Munir — a shining lamp (33:46).

name: Ziyad
note: A classical Arabic name representing blessing and increase in all goodness.

name: Talib
note: Seeking knowledge is an obligation in Islam. Abu Talib was the Prophet's (ﷺ) uncle.

name: Marwan
note: A classical name suggesting firmness and strength of character.

name: Kamil
note: Represents the Islamic aspiration for completeness in faith and character.

name: Badr
note: The Battle of Badr was the first major battle of Islam. The full moon symbolizes beauty and guidance.

name: Dawoud
note: Alternate transliteration of Dawud. Prophet David (عليه السلام).

name: Harith
note: A common pre-Islamic name retained in Islam. Associated with hard work and diligence.

name: Murtada
meaning: Approved, the one who is satisfied
note: A name of Ali ibn Abi Talib (رضي الله عنه) meaning the one with whom Allah is pleased.

name: Nawaf
note: Represents elevation in status, character, and rank.

name: Samir
meaning: Entertaining companion, one who converses at night
note: In Arabic tradition, Samir refers to a companion who entertains with stories.

name: Ubayda
note: Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah (رضي الله عنه), one of the ten promised paradise, the trustee of the Ummah.

name: Waqas
note: Related to Saad ibn Abi Waqqas (رضي الله عنه), one of the ten promised paradise.

name: Yasin
note: Title of Surah 36, sometimes called the heart of the Quran. Often interpreted as a name for the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Zafar
note: A name reflecting triumph and victory, popular across the Muslim world.

name: Ihsan
note: In hadith Jibril, Ihsan is defined as worshipping Allah as if you see Him.

name: Aqil
note: Reflects the importance of reason and wisdom in Islamic thought.

name: Bassam
note: Smiling is a sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said a smile is charity.

name: Dawlat
note: Common in South and Central Asian Muslim communities.

name: Fadl
note: Refers to the grace and bounty of Allah bestowed upon His servants.

name: Hisham
note: A name from a noble Arab tribe. Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik was an Umayyad caliph.

name: Iqbal
note: Muhammad Iqbal (رحمه الله), the great poet-philosopher of the Muslim world.

name: Jibril
meaning: Servant of Allah, mighty one of God
note: Angel Gabriel, the archangel who delivered revelation to the prophets.

name: Mikail
note: Angel Michael, responsible for natural phenomena and sustenance according to Islamic tradition.

name: Raed
note: Represents leadership and being first in exploring new paths.

name: Shafiq
note: Compassion is a central virtue in Islam — the Quran begins with Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.

name: Wadud
note: One of the 99 Names of Allah (Al-Wadud). Refers to deep love and affection.

name: Fatima
note: Daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ) and wife of Ali. The highest-ranking woman in Islam alongside Khadija, Maryam, and Asiya.

name: Aisha
note: Wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), called the Mother of the Believers. One of the greatest scholars of hadith.

name: Khadija
note: First wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), first to accept Islam, the greatest support of the early Muslim community.

name: Maryam
meaning: Beloved, of the sea, pious worshipper
note: Mary, mother of Isa (عليه السلام). The only woman mentioned by name in the Quran; a surah is named after her.

name: Zainab
meaning: Fragrant flower tree, adornment of the father
note: Name of two daughters and a granddaughter of the Prophet (ﷺ), and a wife of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Hafsa
note: Wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), daughter of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Entrusted with the written compilation of the Quran.

name: Ruqayya
note: Daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ). She and her sister Umm Kulthum were both wives of Uthman ibn Affan.

name: Asma
note: Asma bint Abi Bakr (رضي الله عنها), known as Dhāt al-Nitāqayn (She of the Two Belts), daughter of Abu Bakr.

name: Sumayyah
note: The first martyr in Islam. Sumayyah bint Khayyat (رضي الله عنها) was killed for refusing to renounce Islam.

name: Nur
note: Allah is described as the Light of the heavens and the earth (24:35). A beautiful and meaningful name.

name: Safa
note: Al-Safa is one of the two hills in Makkah between which pilgrims walk during Hajj and Umrah.

name: Marwa
note: Al-Marwa is the second of the two sacred hills in Makkah. Running between Safa and Marwa is a rite of Hajj.

name: Layla
meaning: Night, born at night, dark beauty
note: A classic Arabic name. Laylat al-Qadr (Night of Power) is the most blessed night in the Islamic calendar.

name: Amina
note: The name of the Prophet's (ﷺ) beloved mother. She passed away when he was six years old.

name: Safiya
note: Safiya bint Abd al-Muttalib (رضي الله عنها), aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ). Also a wife of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Huda
note: The Quran is described as Huda (guidance) for the believers (2:2). A deeply meaningful name.

name: Iman
note: Iman (faith) is the foundation of Islam, comprising belief in Allah, angels, books, prophets, the Last Day, and divine decree.

name: Nadia
note: Evokes freshness, tenderness, and gentleness — virtues admired in Islamic character.

name: Rania
note: A name suggesting contemplation and wonder, tied to the Islamic practice of reflection (tafakkur).

name: Salma
note: Salma bint Amr, the maternal grandmother of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Tahira
note: A title of Khadija (رضي الله عنها). Purity is central to Islam — 'Cleanliness is half of faith.'

name: Wafaa
note: Faithfulness and fulfilling one's promises are great virtues emphasized in Islam.

name: Yasmin
note: A fragrant flower widely cultivated across the Muslim world. Represents beauty and purity.

name: Zahra
note: Al-Zahra is a title of Fatima, daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning the radiant or resplendent one.

name: Basma
note: Smiling is a sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ). A beautiful name reflecting warmth and kindness.

name: Duaa
note: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Dua is the essence of worship. A deeply spiritual name.

name: Faiza
note: The Quran uses Fauz (triumph) to describe the success of the believers in the hereafter.

name: Ghufran
note: Allah's forgiveness is boundless. The Prophet (ﷺ) constantly sought Allah's forgiveness.

name: Hibah
note: A child is a gift (hibah) from Allah. One of the 99 Names of Allah is Al-Wahhab (the Bestower of Gifts).

name: Jumana
note: A daughter of Abu Sufyan was named Jumanah. The pearl is a symbol of purity and rarity.

name: Khawla
note: Khawla bint Thalaba (رضي الله عنها), whose complaint to Allah is mentioned at the start of Surah Al-Mujadila.

name: Lina
note: Gentleness (lin) is a virtue praised in the Quran and Sunnah. Allah is gentle and loves gentleness.

name: Malak
note: Angels (Malaikah) are honored beings in Islam, created from light, who carry out Allah's commands.

name: Nabila
note: Feminine form of Nabil. Represents nobility of character and virtue.

name: Reem
note: The white gazelle is a symbol of grace and beauty in classical Arabic poetry.

name: Samira
note: Feminine form of Samir. Represents warmth, sociability, and good character.

name: Tasneem
note: Mentioned in the Quran (83:27) as a blessed spring from which the righteous drink in paradise.

name: Ulya
note: Represents loftiness of rank, character, and aspiration — a virtue in Islam.

name: Yara
note: A popular name in Arab and Persian cultures, symbolizing delicacy and beauty.

name: Abeer
note: A name evoking pleasant fragrance. The Prophet (ﷺ) loved good scents.

name: Bayan
note: Allah taught humans eloquence (Bayan) — mentioned in Surah Al-Rahman (55:4).

name: Bushra
meaning: Good news, glad tidings, omen of good
note: Glad tidings are promised to the believers in the Quran (10:64). A joyful and hopeful name.

name: Dina
note: Related to Deen (religion/way of life). Represents commitment to Allah's guidance.

name: Farrukh
note: Common in Central Asian Muslim communities (Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, etc.).

name: Ghada
note: Represents grace and gentle movement. A name popular across the Arab world.

name: Ikram
note: Honoring guests is a highly emphasized virtue in Islam.

name: Jana
note: Evokes the beauty of gathering fruit — a metaphor for the fruits of faith and good deeds.

name: Kawther
note: Surah Al-Kawthar (108) was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), promising him abundant good and a blessed river in Jannah.

name: Lujain
note: Silver is mentioned in the Quran as an adornment of paradise. A name symbolizing purity and value.

name: Manal
note: Represents success in achieving one's goals through effort and trust in Allah.

name: Nada
note: Dew on the morning grass is a symbol of freshness, purity, and Allah's blessings.

name: Ola
note: Represents loftiness and high aspirations in faith and character.

name: Raneem
note: Evokes beautiful sound and melody, often associated with Quranic recitation.

name: Shahd
note: Honey (Asal) is mentioned in the Quran as a cure for people (16:69). A sweet and meaningful name.

name: Thuraya
meaning: The Pleiades star cluster, wealthy, abundant
note: The Pleiades are mentioned in hadith. Named for the beautiful star cluster in the night sky.

name: Widad
note: Islamic brotherhood and love are central to the Muslim community (Ummah).

name: Arwa
note: Arwa bint Abd al-Muttalib (رضي الله عنها), aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Rawda
note: Al-Rawda al-Sharifa is the garden between the Prophet's (ﷺ) grave and his pulpit — a garden of paradise.

name: Yusra
note: The Quran promises: Verily, with hardship comes ease (94:5). A hopeful and comforting name.

name: Lamia
note: A name evoking radiance and brilliance. Light is a central metaphor in the Quran.

name: Omayma
note: A diminutive term of endearment. Omayma bint Abd al-Muttalib was an aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Siham
note: A powerful name evoking precision and strength. Used in classical Arabic poetry.

name: Wajd
note: In Sufi tradition, Wajd refers to the state of spiritual ecstasy in the remembrance of Allah.

name: Zeina
note: Used in the Quran: Tell believing women to lower their gaze... and not display their Zeenah (adornment) (24:31).

name: Nour
note: Variant of Nur. Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth (24:35).

name: Elham
note: Allah inspires the soul with what is right (91:8). A name associated with divine guidance.

name: Hessa
note: Popular in the Gulf region, especially in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

name: Kanza
note: A name evoking preciousness and hidden worth. True treasure in Islam is righteous deeds.

name: Maysaa
note: A classical Arabic name for a woman who walks with dignified grace.

name: Nasreen
note: A flower name popular across Persian, Turkish, and South Asian Muslim communities.

name: Salam
note: As-Salam is one of the 99 Names of Allah. Muslims greet each other with As-Salamu Alaykum (Peace be upon you).

name: Islam
meaning: Submission to Allah, peace through surrender
note: The name of the religion. Rarely used as a personal name but found in some Muslim communities.

name: Rahma
note: The Prophet (ﷺ) was described as a Mercy to all worlds (21:107). A deeply beautiful name.

name: Taqwa
note: Taqwa is the highest virtue in Islam: Verily, the most noble among you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous (49:13).

name: Isra
note: Al-Isra is the miraculous night journey of the Prophet (ﷺ) from Makkah to Jerusalem, referenced in Surah 17.

name: Miraj
note: Al-Miraj was the Prophet's (ﷺ) ascension through the heavens on the night of Isra wal Miraj.

name: Qamar
note: The Quran swears by the moon (Al-Qamar) in multiple surahs. Surah 54 is called Al-Qamar.

name: Shams
note: The Quran swears by the sun in Surah Al-Shams (91:1). Represents brilliance and life-giving energy.

name: Lubna
note: A beautiful classical Arabic name for a type of fragrant tree. Used by the first Muslims.

name: Muna
note: Muna is also the name of the valley near Makkah where pilgrims stay during Hajj.

name: Sana
note: Evokes brightness and the radiance of the divine light that guides believers.

name: Hana
note: Represents the inner happiness and contentment (contentment is a treasure — hadith) of a believer.

name: Insaf
note: Justice (Adl and Insaf) is one of the foundational principles of Islam.

name: Joud
note: The Prophet (ﷺ) was described as the most generous of people. Generosity is highly praised in Islam.

name: Khansa
note: Al-Khansa (رضي الله عنها) was a famous Arab poetess who accepted Islam and lost her four sons at the Battle of Qadisiyya.

name: Nuha
note: Mentioned in the Quran (20:54) as a reference to people of understanding. A deeply meaningful name.

name: Razan
note: Represents the dignity and composure admired in Islamic character.

name: Uzma
note: Reflects supreme greatness. Refers to Allah's majesty (Al-Azim, the Most Great).

name: Wadha
note: Evokes clarity and brightness, as in the clear white light of the moon.

name: Zumurrud
note: Emeralds are mentioned in the Quran as adornments of paradise. A name of beauty and rarity.

name: Tawba
note: Allah is Al-Tawwab (the Accepter of Repentance). Surah 9 is called Surah Al-Tawba.

name: Shuruq
note: Represents new beginnings and the light of a new day — a symbol of hope in Islam.

name: Amin
note: Al-Amin was the title given to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) by the people of Makkah.

name: Sadiq
note: As-Sadiq was a title of the Prophet (ﷺ). Truthfulness is one of the pillars of good character in Islam.

name: Hayat
note: Allah is Al-Hayy (the Ever-Living). Life is a trust from Allah to be spent in His service.

name: Farah
note: The joy of a believer is in remembering Allah and living righteously.

name: Riham
note: Rain is a mercy from Allah (7:57). Gentle rain symbolizes blessings and sustenance.

name: Hiba
note: Children are a gift from Allah. One of the 99 Names of Allah is Al-Wahhab (the Giver of Gifts).

name: Dua
note: Variant spelling of Duaa. The weapon of the believer and the essence of worship.

name: Muntaha
meaning: The utmost limit, the furthest end
note: Sidrat al-Muntaha is the tree at the furthest boundary of the heavens, beyond which no creation can pass.

name: Huzaifa
note: Hudhaifa ibn al-Yaman (رضي الله عنه), a close Companion entrusted with knowledge of the hypocrites.

name: Sad
note: Alternate shorter form of Saad. Also the name of a Quranic surah (Surah 38, Sad).

name: Khair
note: The Quran frequently uses Khayr to describe the good of this world and the next.

name: Bara
note: Bara ibn Azib (رضي الله عنه) was a Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Salwa
note: Al-Salwa is the quail that Allah sent as food from heaven for the Children of Israel (2:57).

name: Asiya
note: Asiya bint Muzahim (رضي الله عنها), the wife of Pharaoh, is one of the four greatest women in Islam.

name: Halima
note: Halima al-Sadiyya (رضي الله عنها), the foster mother who nursed the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

name: Suhaib
note: Suhaib ibn Sinan al-Rumi (رضي الله عنه), a Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ) known for his sacrifice for Islam.

name: Suhayb
note: Alternate transliteration of Suhaib. The same beloved Companion of the Prophet (ﷺ).

name: Mukhtar
note: Al-Mukhtar (the Chosen) is a title of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Means divinely chosen and selected.
